Featured project

Policy Insurance Analysis Dashboard

AI Variant Data Analyst Internship (ExcelR programme) · Jun 2026 – Sep 2026 · Excel, Power BI, Tableau, MySQL

This project analyzes a portfolio of 5,000 insurance policies to answer practical questions: how many policies are still active, how the policy types and customer groups compare, and how premiums have moved over time. I took it from raw data to finished dashboards: loading and structuring the data, querying it in MySQL, and presenting the results in three BI tools.

The goal was one consistent set of KPIs. I built the same dashboard in Excel, Power BI and Tableau and cross-checked every figure, so the numbers are identical on all three platforms.

33.64%Active share
0.51 : 1Active-to-inactive
14.53%Premium growth diff.

How the project was built

1 · Understand

Problem & scope

Define what to measure
  • Questions: how many policies are active, lapsed or terminated; how policy types, age groups and genders compare; and how premiums and claims change over time.
  • Scope: 5,000 policy records and 5,000 customers, across Auto, Health, Life and Property policies.
2 · ETL

Extract, clean & load

Preparing the data
  • Extracted the raw policy data and checked it for missing values, duplicates and inconsistent formats.
  • Standardized fields such as policy type, status and dates so they could be grouped reliably.
  • Loaded the cleaned data into MySQL, ready for modelling and querying.
3 · Model

Relational model

Five linked tables
  • CustomerInfo: customer ID, name, gender, age, occupation, marital status and address — one record per customer.
  • PolicyDetails: policy type, coverage and premium amount, start/end dates, payment frequency and status, linked to a customer.
  • Claims: claim ID, date, amount, status, reason and settlement date, linked to a policy.
  • Payment History: individual payments — amount paid, method, status and date, linked to a policy.
  • Additional Fields: agent ID, renewal status, policy discounts and risk score, linked to a policy.
4 · Query

SQL analysis

MySQL techniques
  • Joins to link CustomerInfo, PolicyDetails, Claims, Payment History and Additional Fields.
  • Aggregations for counts by type and status, average premium and coverage, and total claims.
  • CASE WHEN to group customers into age bands (18–25 up to 65+) and label statuses.
  • CTEs to build the calculations step by step and keep the queries readable.
  • Window functions to compare each year with the previous one and get premium growth rates.
5 · Visualize

Dashboards

One KPI set, three tools
  • Excel: pivot-based dashboard with slicers.
  • Tableau: brown-theme dashboard with policy type, status and year filters.
  • Power BI: blue-theme dashboard with a year slicer and Show All / Hide All navigation.
  • Each shows KPI cards, policy counts by type, status and age group, average premium and coverage, and yearly trends.
6 · Validate

Cross-validation

Checking every number
  • Compared every KPI card and chart total across Excel, Power BI and Tableau.
  • Fixed any difference at its source until all figures matched: 5,000 policies, 33.64% active, 14.53% premium growth difference, 251M in claims.
  • This is what "100% KPI consistency" means: the same answer on every platform.
Insights

Key findings

What the data shows
  • Policy mix is balanced: Health leads with 1,316 policies and Auto is lowest with 1,214, a gap of 102.
  • Only 33.64% of policies are active (1,682). Lapsed (1,640) and terminated (1,678) together outnumber them, a 0.51 : 1 ratio.
  • Older customers dominate: the 65+ group has 1,408 policies; 18–25 has 572.
  • Premiums are falling: average premium dropped from 1,216 (2014) to 991 (2024). Best year: 2022 (+4.79%). Worst: 2015 (−9.74%).
  • Life policies have the highest averages: premium 1,085 and coverage 259,037.
  • Gender split is close: "Other" is highest at 1,699, with a difference of 53.
Takeaways

What it shows

Skills demonstrated
  • End-to-end analytics: ETL, relational modelling, SQL, dashboards and validation.
  • Delivering the same insights in Excel, Power BI and Tableau.
  • Turning raw numbers into findings a business can act on.

Featured project: HR Analytics

HR Analytics Dashboard Suite — Arvexa Tech

HR Analytics internship project · 2021–2025 data · Excel, Tableau, Power BI, MySQL

This project answers 67 workforce questions for Arvexa Tech, a company with 2,299 employees in the dataset: how headcount is moving, who is leaving and why, how people perform, how engaged they are, and what pay and training cost. The data comes from 18 linked HR tables covering employees, exits, performance, surveys, payroll, recruitment and training.

The 67 KPIs were split across four tools with no repetition: 17 in Excel, 17 in Tableau, 17 in Power BI and 16 in MySQL. Each one was checked against an answer key for 2024 and 2025, and shared definitions (such as attrition = exits ÷ average headcount) were used in every tool.

How it was built

Excel

17-KPI dashboard

Pivots, slicers and charts
  • One dashboard with 17 visuals: span of control, work-from-office compliance, exits by year, tenure, retention, notice period served and more.
  • HireDate, WorkMode, Year and JobLevel slicers filter every visual.
  • Navigation button and consistent card layout.
Tableau

17 KPIs, six dashboards

Calculated fields and navigation
  • Overview, Workforce, Attrition, Attendance, Hiring and Engagement dashboards, with a sidebar of icon buttons.
  • Growth arrows turn green or red from a calculated field, so the colour follows the value.
  • Department, Job Level and Location filters; a download button and an About button linking to the HR overview page.
Power BI

17 DAX KPIs, six pages

Measures, a year axis and a navigator
  • A relational model with the Employees table at the centre and the dimension tables around it.
  • One measure per KPI, driven by a selected-year measure, so the same measure serves the cards, the charts and the matrix.
  • Six KPI cards with year-on-year arrows, four multi-year charts, an 8-row KPI matrix, and a page navigator.
MySQL

16 KPI queries

Recruitment, pay and learning
  • Loaded all 18 sheets into MySQL with a Python script that keeps dates as real DATE columns.
  • Joins, conditional aggregation and helper views (years and average headcount).
  • 15 of 16 queries reproduce the answer key for 2024 and 2025.

What the data shows

  • Attrition fell sharply, then edged up. It dropped from 19.3% in 2022 to 12.2% in 2024, and rose to 13.5% in 2025. Voluntary exits drive it: 11.5% against 1.9% involuntary.
  • The exits that hurt are growing. Regrettable exits rose from 16.0% of voluntary exits in 2021 to 27.3% in 2025.
  • Customer Success loses the most people (18.5% in 2025), ahead of Sales and Business Development (16.5%).
  • Pay is catching up with the market bands. Median compa-ratio climbed from 0.81 in 2021 to 0.98 in 2025.
  • Promotions are slowing. The average time since an employee's last promotion rose from 0.8 years in 2021 to 2.6 years in 2025.
  • Performance is improving. High performers went from 32.5% to 39.2% over the same period.
